review: Frau von Arnstein (a Viennese concert-goer, 1788): I am pleased that the phrases close properly, with honest cadences; the voices move with propriety; the melody sits squarely on the beat; the harmonies are such as any good master would write. I struggled to follow a clear tune.

slider.label: a classical piece with tidbits of the song

layers.text: Only the skeleton of the tune is kept (its strong-beat notes). The notes in between are re-composed as classical scale passages.
The bass is re-written as a period bass line (walking, Alberti or sustained).
The original backing is replaced by the composer's own accompaniment textures over (re-)harmonised chords.
No drums. The rhythm comes from the accompaniment, as in real classical music.

era.name: Classical
era.summary: Clear, balanced phrases with a singable tune on top and light, transparent accompaniment, where every phrase ends in a satisfying cadence.
traits: Homophony: one main melody with accompaniment beneath
Crescendos and contrasts of mood within a movement
The string quartet and the symphony orchestra take their classic shape
era.instruments: String quartet, fortepiano, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, horns, trumpets, timpani
why: All three eras were tried. Classical scored best (Classical 1.236, Baroque 1.235, Romantic 1.164). The score combines how classical it sounds, how much of the song survives, and how well the song suits the composer.
The song is built from regular 4- and 8-bar phrases. That matches the Classical era's balanced question-and-answer phrasing, so cadences fit naturally at phrase ends.

composer.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart

reasons: its fairly even energy suits a steady, unbroken style
applied: Inner strings murmur repeated eighth notes under the tune, the classic Viennese accompaniment

ensemble.name: String quartet
ensemble.summary: Two violins, viola and cello. The Classical era's favourite chamber group.
why: It is one of Mozart's favourite settings.
In this composer's style it scored best of the four ensembles: String quartet 1.236, Chamber ensemble 1.164, Orchestra 1.163, Solo keyboard 1.141.
Why it works: four equal voices give clean voice-leading and a warm, blended, unmistakably classical sound.
The violin carries the vocal melody (F#4–A5). It was moved by octaves into the instrument's most singing register, with the key unchanged.

parts.what: First violin sings the vocal line
Second violin fills in harmony or plays a counter-line

changes.ending: It follows the original beat by beat and lasts exactly as long as the clip (19.1s).
changes.dropped: The drum kit, synths and electric bass are gone. Their rhythmic drive now comes from the accompaniment patterns.
